candidates.change_summary: Replace the addition order when updating balances so that msg.value is added on the right-hand side (no functional change) — REJECTED as equivalent, so instead changed assert to require to alter revert behavior on overflow check.
Remove the overflow check assert, allowing zero-value deposits to be accepted and avoiding an assert revert on overflow condition.
Negate the comparison so the guard requires that msg.value be zero or negative (impossible), causing all deposits with positive value to revert.
Move the decrement of the sender balance to occur before the external transfer (pre-decrement), changing reentrancy safety and observable balance after withdraw.

Use send() instead of transfer(), which returns a boolean and alters behavior on failure (here we ignore the return), potentially changing observable transfer outcome and state when transfer would revert.

Change the order to transfer first then decrement balance (as in original) but use call.value-style low-level call that returns success, leaving balance unchanged on failure — using (bool, ) = msg.sender.call{value: amount}(""); to alter observable behavior on failure.
Remove the balance decrement entirely so balances are not reduced after withdraw, changing subsequent observable behavior.
Change the recipient of the transfer from the provided address to the creator, so migrateTo sends the contract balance to creator instead of to parameter 'to'.
Require that msg.sender equals the provided 'to' address instead of requiring msg.sender be the creator, changing who can call migrateTo.

Insert a statement that zeroes the creator address before transfer, making the transfer go to the (now zeroed) creator address when using creator as recipient after the insert would change behavior; here we zero creator and still transfer to 'to', altering observable creator state only if external reads of creator are observed before/after.
Transfer only half of the contract balance to 'to' instead of the full balance.
